A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIO research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material relocated in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original MIO evaluations for image, speech, and video tasks in Tables 3–6, alongside qualitative demonstrations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds language-only, trimodal, speech-to-speech, human-evaluation, and tokenizer-ablation results.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the Yi backbone, SEED-Tokenizer and SpeechTokenizer, speech-codebook handling, causal objective, masked packing, and three pre-training stages followed by SFT. The VQGAN alternatives in v3 are ablation configurations, not replacements in the proposed model.

E1.justification: v3 adds MMLU evaluation, simultaneous text-image-speech comprehension on OmniBench, and speech-to-speech conversations converted from moss-002-sft. TTS coverage expands to GLOBE and LibriSpeech test-clean; LibriSpeech previously supplied ASR evaluation. Training datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Qwen-VL-Chat and LLaVA 1.5. New comparisons include LLaMA-1/2 on MMLU, Gemini-1.5-Pro, Reka-Core, video-SALMONN and Unified-IO 2 on OmniBench, and LLaMA-Omni for speech-to-speech. Table 4's shortened SEED-LLaMA name retains the previous scores and does not establish a different comparator.

E3.justification: New protocols include zero-shot MMLU, four-option trimodal evaluation, a controlled 3K-step tokenizer comparison, SSIM/aesthetic scoring, and human ranking of images from 100 COCO descriptions. v3 also introduces GPT-4o speech-response grading and additional TTS evaluations without voice prompts, using speaker similarity and human preferences. Existing benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 3.6/Figure 2 adds a qualitative SEED-versus-VQGAN tokenizer ablation, while Appendix E.4/Figure 3 adds stagewise training-loss analysis. These examine tokenizer choice and training dynamics beyond the retained preliminary speech-interleaving observations. The CoT demonstration also changes its displayed input image while retaining its answer.

E5.justification: v3 introduces three-annotator image-ranking agreement and averaging across three independent TTS evaluators. Neither version reports model-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The reported 82.3% image-ranking agreement does not reconcile with the stated formula counting unanimous cases out of 100.

E6.justification: Existing scores in Tables 3–6 remain unchanged, but v3 adds baseline rows and substantial new results. MIO scores 45.7 on MMLU and 36.96 on OmniBench. Speech-to-speech content scores favor LLaMA-Omni (2.4) and AnyGPT (1.8) over MIO (1.4), whereas GLOBE TTS WER favors MIO (9.8 versus 27.9). These are newly reported evaluations, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The causal training objective in Equation 1 and existing mathematical reasoning are unchanged. Added explanations of standard evaluation metrics introduce no new theoretical definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about four-modality understanding/generation, multimodal interleaved output, competitive performance, and emergent capabilities. Additional experiments support or qualify these retained claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 removes v2 Appendix A's explicit limitations concerning OCR/detail loss, uncontrollable timbre, and inability to generate continuous raw video, without documenting fixes. It adds interpretations concerning dual-to-trimodal generalization, tokenizer semantics and convergence, training-loss recovery, and weaker speech-to-speech scores under direct speech generation.

D1.justification: v3 adds tokenizer configurations and source links for the VQGAN comparison, Aesthetic Predictor v2.5, and MOSS data, plus implementation choices for new evaluations. Existing training/SFT hyperparameters, decoding settings, and MIO code/model access information are retained.

R1.justification: References expand to cover MMLU, OmniBench, LLaMA-Omni, LLaMA-1/2, GLOBE, and image-quality evaluation, among others. Lu et al.'s Chameleon: Plug-and-play compositional reasoning reference is removed. The principal modeling taxonomy and novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most core prose and the main section order are retained. v3 makes local wording, terminology, and affiliation edits, switches to author-year citations, adds experiment subsections, and reorganizes appendix headings; it does not extensively rewrite the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds six result tables and tokenizer/loss figures, expands Table 3, and substantially reformats the document. Main-text demonstrations move to Appendix E.5 and receive new colors and legends. v2 Figure 4's bubble-gum/spring image becomes a different four-panel illustration in v3 Figure 6 despite retaining the question and answer.

improvement.justification: The new trimodal, speech-to-speech, and human evaluations address important validation gaps and expose both strengths and weaknesses. However, v3 removes concrete capability limitations, introduces an unexplained CoT image/answer mismatch in Figure 6, and reports annotator agreement inconsistent with its stated calculation in Appendix E.1. These transparency and reporting problems leave the net quality effect of the broader evidence uncertain.
